content:
elaine: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — RCA is posted: https://redwood.internal/rca/INC-2026-451 :link:  TL;DR: a cascade of cache-evictions + model-shard throttling caused router pod CPU run-queue spikes -> timeouts for warm-start requests. Action items below, please ack owners.

elaine: Action items (short):
• maya - update runbook (add cache eviction play, add rollback steps)
• raj - add 2nd-level alert on router_runq_size and link to dashboard
• jonathan - add synthetic that exercises prefix/KV cache eviction in CI
• liz - propose infra change (router CPU limit + pod suiting) by EOD Thurs
• sam - customer comms draft for impacted Dedicated tenants
• eng-oncall - validate cross-region fallback configs

raj: Ack. I'll take the alert and dashboard link. Can someone paste the exact metric name? I saw two similar ones in grafana. :eyes:

elaine: The one that tripped was `router_cpu_runq_seconds` (histogram) and the derived `router_runq_p99`. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/board/5?var-region=us-east

sam: Were only Dedicated customers affected, or hosted as well?

elaine: Mostly Dedicated in us-east (burst pools). Hosted traffic fell back to regional read replicas so partial degradation. We'll call out the tenant list in the comms draft. @sam please coordinate with support for the exact list.

maya: I'll pick up the runbook. Plan: add a pre-flight checklist for cache-busting deploys, include a runbook step to `scale-down evictor` and `pause-schedulers` before rolling shards. Will open PR today. :woman_technologist:

jonathan: Strong +1 for a synthetic. I can add a nightly job that forces a controlled eviction and measures tail-latency. Will add a note to the test ticket: https://phab.redwood/T1234

liz: For infra, I want to propose two changes: bump router CPU request to 2 vCPU (from 0.5) for the warm path, and add a pod anti-affinity rule to spread routers across hosts. I'll write a short RFC and cost estimate by EOD Thurs. Anyone opposed to trying that as an immediate mitigation? :thinking:

raj: No objections. We should also consider an automated scale trigger when `router_runq_p95` > 0.7 for 3m.

devops-bot: Deployment queued: `hotfix/router-fallback-2026-03-xx` — started canary in us-east-1, 3/10 pods. CI: https://ci.redwood/build/8842

sam: Thanks @devops-bot. After canary completes, can we pause rollouts and run synthetic? want to validate before full rollout.

elaine: Yes — canary -> synthetic -> rollout. Also note: schedule a postmortem sync with SRE + infra + platform tomorrow 11am PT. I'll put calendar invite.

maya: acked, will include playbook diff in PR and tag `eng-oncall` for review.

jonathan: Added test skeleton and example script to the ticket, will link PR here when ready.

liz: I'll include rough cost delta in RFC. If we can't afford permanent bump, we can do an autoscale policy change with higher burst headroom.

raj: Quick q for leadership: do we want to change the default canary duration for shard-rollouts? current is 15m. That felt short for this class of failure.

elaine: Good call — let's increase default canary to 1h for shard and cache-affecting rollouts. I'll update the rollout policy doc tomorrow and notify release engineering.

sam: I'll draft the customer communication and post here for review before sending.

maya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/runbooks/pull/489 — runbook changes + play steps.

elaine: Thank you everyone — please mark items done in the action tracker: https://tracker.redwood/actions?filter=INC-2026-451. We'll re-check in the sprint planning meeting next Tues. :thumbsup:

raj: Acked and picking alert as owner.

jonathan: Will follow up with synthetic results next week.

liz: RFC incoming. Thanks.

sam: Draft will be up in 2 hours.

elaine: Closing the thread here. If you need to discuss implications for Dedicated SLAs or billing mitigations, ping me directly and I'll loop in sales. Appreciate the quick responses. :pray:
